inline.s: Spiritual response and communion: the subjective influence of sentient beings and the response of Amitābha Buddha mutually reach and interpenetrate each other.
The original says:
The recitation rests on me; the welcoming and guidance rest on the Buddha.
The answer is: therefore when I recite, I must be in spiritual response and communion with the Buddha, so as to receive the Buddha's welcome and guidance.
The original says:
“Do not go finding fault for no reason, forever suspecting and fretting over this matter of whether scattered-mind recitation can attain rebirth.”

The answer is: whether a path can lead to rebirth is a matter of the greatest importance! If you do not get it clear and are dragged confused into the fire pit, to gain a human body again, to hear the Dharma again, to cultivate the Pure Land again — who knows which eon and which life that will be! Do you still wish to suffer in this endless long night, with unremitting pain and torment? And when that time comes, whom will you blame?

[Original]Scattered-mind recitation is quite normal; precisely because there are deluded thoughts, one recites. For one who constantly calls the Buddha's name, scattering naturally stills, the deluded mind naturally ceases, the three karmas naturally harmonize, and the vow-mind naturally arises. No one lives out a hundred years, yet all harbor a thousand years of worry. Scattered-mind recitation is still better than none at all; but to be able to recite with a focused mind is of course even better.
[Comment]

Does scattered-mind recitation achieve “scattering naturally stills, the deluded mind naturally ceases, the three karmas naturally harmonize, and the vow-mind naturally arises”? That is why the patriarchs of the Pure Land school down the ages all taught:
recite with one mind.
For example,
Master Tanluan's Teachings on the Pure Land
Master Daochuo's Teachings on Pure Practice
and
Master Shandao's Pure Land Teachings

. Scattered-mind recitation is of course better than no recitation, for one has planted a diamond seed, which will in the end flower and bear fruit; but in this life one may not necessarily attain rebirth (see in detail
Does Scattered-Mind Recitation Also Necessarily Attain Rebirth?
[Original]But then, who has the final say on the conditions for rebirth?
Of course the Buddha has the final say, and the scriptures are the standard!
[Comment]
Utterly correct; of course the Buddha has the final say on the conditions for rebirth, and the scriptures are the standard!

I hope you will earnestly study the Pure Land scriptures and the patriarchs' commentaries on them, and not give ear to those fallacious and heretical theories that wrench passages out of context or are invented out of nothing. For example, concerning the ten recitations of Amitābha's original vow (the Eighteenth Vow), the patriarchs and great masters through the ages have all taught:
these are the ten recitations, continuous, at the end of life.
— this is the condition for rebirth.
(See in detail
The Eighteenth Vow
On the meaning of the Eighteenth Vow, Master Daochuo taught in the Collection of Peace and Bliss:
“If there are sentient beings who, even if they commit evil throughout an entire life,
at the end of life, with ten continuous recitations
, call upon my name,
and if they do not attain rebirth, I will not attain perfect enlightenment.”
Here, Master Daochuo gives a precise explanation of the meaning of “even down to ten recitations” in the Eighteenth Vow:
at the end of life, with ten continuous recitations, call upon my name.
Therefore, “even down to ten recitations” in the Eighteenth Vow refers to the ten recitations at the end of life, and moreover to continuous recitations.
Continuity: not being interrupted by deluded thoughts. Master Tanluan's Commentary on the Treatise on Rebirth says:
“thought after thought in continuity, with no other thought mixed in
(no other thought mixed in)
Master Tanluan also says:
no other thought mixing in
(no other thought intermingled)
, thought after thought in succession, up to ten recitations,
this is called continuity in ten recitations
(A Brief Treatise on the Meaning of the Pure Land of Peace and Bliss)
As for the condition for rebirth
Master Shandao taught:
“It is precisely because calling the name is easy
(precisely because calling the name in recitation is easier than visualizing and contemplating the Buddha)
, that with continuity one is born there
(at the end of life, if one but achieves the continuity of the thought of recitation (not interrupted by deluded thoughts), one attains rebirth in the Western Pure Land of Ultimate Bliss)
. If one can keep the thought continuous, recitation after recitation, to the end of one's life
(a person who practices thus for a whole lifetime)
, ten of ten are born, hundred of hundred are born.”
(See in detail
Master Shandao's Pure Land Teachings
Master Shandao is a manifestation of Amitābha Buddha; his words are the words of Amitābha Buddha, so of course he has the final say on the conditions for rebirth
Master Yongming is also
a manifestation of Amitābha Buddha; on the condition for rebirth he taught:
one must, with a mind of continuous recitation, accomplish the ten recitations at the end of life.
Master Yongming says:
If words and actions do not correspond
(if words and deeds do not match)
and the power of faith is slight, without
a mind of continuous recitation

, but with the intent of breaking off again and again, relying on this indolence and hoping for rebirth at the end of life, one is only obstructed by karmic hindrances; I fear it will be hard to meet a good spiritual friend, and under the pressing of wind and fire, right mindfulness is not accomplished. Why? Now is the cause, and the end of life is the fruit; one should make the cause real, then the fruit will not be empty. If one would
accomplish the ten recitations at the end of life
, one should make ready the crossing, gather the accumulated merit, and dedicate it to that time
(dedicate to the time of death)
; then, thought after thought without loss, there is nothing to worry about.”
(The Collection of the Return of All Good)
This is entirely consistent with Master Shandao's teaching.

Master Yongming is also a manifestation of Amitābha Buddha: Because Master Yongming is a manifestation of Amitābha Buddha, his birthday, the seventeenth day of the eleventh lunar month, is observed as the celebration of Amitābha Buddha's birthday. Of Master Yongming, Master Yinguang praised:
“Master Yongming is an incarnation of Amitābha Buddha. With great compassion and great mercy he opens and transforms sentient beings.”
(The Collected Writings of Master Yinguang
Dharma Talks at the World Buddhist Lay Association)

Accomplishment of the ten recitations at the end of life: to accomplish the ten continuous recitations at the end of life. Making ready the crossing: “the crossing” means the ferry and the bridge; “making ready the crossing” means to prepare for it well in advance.

As the saying goes: “To know the way into the mountains, one must ask the one who has been there.” Master Tanluan and Master Daochuo are people who cultivated and realized the fruit; they are the ones who have been there on the path of rebirth.
As for the condition for rebirth
Masters Tanluan and Daochuo taught:
with the ten recitations at the end of life, if continuous, one is born there.
(See in detail
Master Tanluan's Teachings on the Pure Land
Master Daochuo's Teachings on Pure Practice
and
The Ten Recitations at the End of Life: Continuous, then Born
This is entirely consistent with the teachings of Master Shandao and Master Yongming.
You do not heed the words of Amitābha Buddha, nor the words of the great patriarchs, yet you give ear to that wild and random talk, and so ruin your own great matter of rebirth. Whom will you blame?
[Original]
Ordinary beings must absolutely not draw a line on the ground to limit themselves, saying: those who recite with a scattered mind cannot attain rebirth
[Comment]
“those who recite with a scattered mind cannot attain rebirth”

this statement is not accurate. The accurate statement is: scattered-mind recitation does not definitively attain rebirth. That is to say, scattered-mind recitation may not necessarily attain rebirth.
For one who normally recites with a scattered mind,

if at the end of life one achieves ten continuous recitations, one can likewise attain rebirth. This is why there is assistance at the time of death. Assisting at death is helping the dying person to raise right mindfulness, to maintain right mindfulness, and to achieve ten continuous recitations. If at death deluded thoughts fly about in confusion, then one flows along with one's karma.

One must pay special attention: the possibility that one who normally recites with a scattered mind should at death achieve ten continuous recitations is extremely slight; the patriarchs and great masters down the ages have all taught on this. For example, Master Daochuo taught:
“The wise diligently gather the mind
(reciting with one mind in daily life)
, so that at death the mind is not scattered; one unaccustomed to focusing the mind
(recites with a scattered mind in daily life)
, will surely be scattered at death.”
(See in detail
Master Daochuo's Teachings on Pure Practice
) Master Yongming taught:
Now is the cause, and the end of life is the fruit; one should make the cause real, then the fruit will not be empty.
If one would accomplish the ten recitations at the end of life, one should make ready the crossing
(make thorough preparation in advance)
, gather the accumulated merit, and dedicate it to that time
(dedicate to the time of death)
; then, thought after thought without loss, there is nothing to worry about.”
(The Collection of the Return of All Good

[Original]The Pure Land practice of recitation was originally meant to open wide the Dharma-door to those who recite with a scattered mind. Let me ask: in this whole world, who can recite with a focused mind? Among us lay people, who can set everything down cleanly and completely, or easily gain the samādhi of Buddha-recitation?
Is the samādhi of Buddha-recitation really the main condition for rebirth?
[Comment]The Pure Land practice of recitation
is not
opening wide the Dharma-door to those who recite with a scattered mind, but to those who recite with a focused mind
The condition for rebirth is not the samādhi of Buddha-recitation
, but right mindfulness at the end of life (see in detail
Right Mindfulness at the End of Life
and
Right Mindfulness at the End of Life: Replies to Questions
. In daily life
a focused, undisturbed mind is the reliable guarantee of right mindfulness at the end of life.
The samādhi of Buddha-recitation is the illumination of the mind and the seeing of one's nature through recitation, far higher than the state of a focused, undisturbed mind (see in detail
Verifying the Samādhi of Buddha-Recitation

The universal path, in order to end birth and death and escape transmigration, must pass through the myriad thoughts returning to one, the one returning to nothing, the illumination of the mind and seeing of one's own nature, then the practice of maintaining, until the delusions of views and thought are cut off entirely; only then can one end birth and death and escape transmigration. Therefore
a focused, undisturbed mind (
the myriad thoughts returning to one
) is but the initial stage of practice; as long as the method is correct and one
diligently and untiringly
works at it, everyone can reach it.

Hence the saying: of ten thousand who cultivate, ten thousand go. The key of “of ten thousand who cultivate, ten thousand go” lies in cultivating — cultivating correctly, cultivating diligently and untiringly!

In fact, a focused, undisturbed mind is not beyond reach. From ancient times on through the Ming and Qing dynasties, Buddhism in China was mainly Chan; therefore many Chan practitioners wrongly held that reciting with a focused, undisturbed mind to attain rebirth in the Western Pure Land is an expedient method set up for people of dull faculties. And many of those who cultivated the Pure Land practiced mainly the samādhi of Buddha-recitation and the pratyutpanna samādhi, so a focused, undisturbed mind was nothing worth mentioning. How is it that now a focused, undisturbed mind is spoken of as high above the clouds and looked on as a fearful path? In the sutras, treatises, and the records and sayings of the Chan school, there are countless methods and instances of reaching the myriad thoughts returning to one and focusing the mind on a single point; why not study and practice them? Why belittle oneself, declaring oneself good for nothing, and even casting away one's own Buddha-nature, identical to that of all Buddhas? For example, the original says:

“Ordinary beings are in their substance entirely deluded thought, like a clay statue of a man; even ground down to the last grain, it is still clay. How much more so when the body is sunk in the five turbid worlds and the land is impure — how can the mind be pure? Can grinding a brick make a mirror? How can iron ore be refined out of wood?”

Cultivating the samādhi of Buddha-recitation: cultivating the samādhi of Buddha-recitation is mindful holding through principle, reciting the Buddha of one's own nature (the Amitābha of one's own nature) to see through to the original face. The eighth patriarch of the Pure Land school, Master Lianchi (Zhuhong), says:

“Know that the Pure Land is mind-only; there is no external realm.” “In accord with principle, then one's own nature returns to the original substance; this is the meaning of vowing to be born in that land.” “Reciting the Buddha is reciting the mind; being born there does not depart from being born here. Mind, Buddha, and sentient beings are one substance, abiding neither on the middle current nor on either shore. Hence it is called the Amitābha of one's own nature, the mind-only Pure Land.”

(The Commentary on the Amitābha Sūtra). The pratyutpanna samādhi, also called the samādhi of the Buddha standing, means that the one who cultivates this samādhi and attains accomplishment can see the Buddhas of the ten directions standing before him. In practice, one neither sits nor lies down, from morning to night and from night to morning, either walking or standing, taking ninety days as one period, and single-mindedly recites the name of Amitābha Buddha.
[Original]
Let us still believe in the vow of Amitābha Buddha: even with one thought or ten recitations one can be welcomed and guided by the Buddha.
[Comment]The
one thought or ten recitations”
— its meaning must be heeded according to the teachings and instructions of the patriarchs down the ages:
this is a single thought or ten recitations at the end of life, unmingled with deluded thoughts
see in detail
The Original Vow of Amitābha
the article
For example, Master Yinguang taught:

“In the Contemplation Sūtra, one guilty of the five deadly offences and the ten evil deeds, about to die, with the signs of hell appearing, has a good spiritual friend (original note: this does not distinguish monk or lay, man or woman; whoever can teach him to recite the Buddha is called a good spiritual friend) who teaches him to recite the Buddha — perhaps only ten sounds, perhaps not even ten sounds, and then he directly dies; even so, by relying on the Buddha's compassionate power, he attains rebirth still bearing his karma. These ten recitations, compared with ordinary ten recitations, have a fierce and urgent power differing as heaven from the deep; hence he attains rebirth. Because he is pressed by the extreme suffering of hell, upon first hearing the Buddha's name he recites it with his whole mind and spirit.
Beyond this recitation there is absolutely no other thought.
Though he has not personally realized the focused, undisturbed mind, still his mind in the end has no differing thought at all.
The Collected Writings of Master Yinguang, Third Compilation
Volume Two
Letter in Reply to Lay Believer Chen Xinru
[Original]We must be mindful without letting go (thinking of the Buddha, reciting the Buddha), with the end of life as our term. Recite the single Buddha-name to the very end. Whether for
days, whether for
years, whether for
years.
[Comment]
mindful without letting go (thinking of the Buddha, reciting the Buddha)

, then this is not scattered-mind recitation but a focused-minded recitation! Scattered-mind recitation is: reciting while still giving rise to deluded thoughts. In those moments of delusion there is no recitation or thinking of the Buddha; that is a letting go. So the patriarchs say:
thought after thought in continuity, with the end of life as the term.

That is to say, the thought of recitation must continue one after another, unmingled in between with deluded thoughts. If one truly achieves “thought after thought in continuity, with the end of life as the term,” then that is excellent! Ten of ten are born; hundred of hundred are born.
[Original]Nor do we practice in mixture any other Dharma-doors of the Buddhas and bodhisattvas.
[Comment]
nor do we practice in mixture any other Dharma-doors of the Buddhas and bodhisattvas”
, is quite correct; but along the way of practice one must not be misled by a blind teacher.
[Original]Deeply and well enter into Master Shandao's teaching, for after all he is the patriarch universally acknowledged as a manifestation of Amitābha Buddha!
[Comment]This statement is most correct! But one must pay special attention: Master Shandao said
with continuity, one is born
, not that scattered-mind recitation necessarily attains rebirth. (By the way, if scattered-mind recitation necessarily attained rebirth, why would one still need assistance at the time of death?)
Master Shandao, a manifestation of Amitābha Buddha, taught:
“It is precisely because calling the name is easy
(precisely because calling the name in recitation is easier than visualizing and contemplating the Buddha)
, that with continuity one is born there
(at the end of life, if one but achieves the continuity of the thought of recitation (not interrupted by deluded thoughts), one attains rebirth in the Western Pure Land of Ultimate Bliss)
. If one can keep the thought continuous, recitation after recitation, to the end of one's life
(a person who practices thus for a whole lifetime)
, ten of ten are born, hundred of hundred are born.”
(See in detail
Master Shandao's Pure Land Teachings

[Original]As long as one can reach the shore, the breaststroke, the freestyle, or even the dog paddle will do. Don't mind whether the mind is scattered or not; in any case, single-mindedly calling the name is what counts. Ordinary beings must not presumptuously speculate!

[Comment]Though swimming across a river does not care about the stroke, one must still be able to swim and reach the shore, otherwise one drowns in the river. So a recitation practitioner must at the end of life maintain right mindfulness; with continuity, one is born (see in detail
Master Shandao's Pure Land Teachings
Question: Now there are some organizations and websites that use the name “Pure Land school”
, for example the Pure Land school Hongyuan Temple, the Pure Land school
Pure Land school Portal
China Pure Land school
Global Pure Land school Portal Website, the Chinese Pure Land school Association, and the like
— what is this about?
Answer: This is all the doing of Master Huijing of the Original-Vow Dharma-door
(for background on this person, see in detail
What Is the Original-Vow Dharma-door?

The term Pure Land school originally referred to the sect among the ten schools of Buddhism that specializes in reciting the Buddha to seek rebirth in the Western Pure Land of Ultimate Bliss, with Master Huiyuan of the Jin dynasty as its first patriarch,
a great sect standing side by side with the Chan school for a thousand years

. Yet their Original-Vow Dharma-door is but a small school, and Master Huijing actually names it the “Pure Land school,” as though they were the entire Pure Land school! This is a deliberate creation of confusion, passing off fish eyes as pearls and the false for the true, so as to deceive those who do not know the facts — especially beginning students of Buddhism — into mistakenly thinking they are the Pure Land school and boarding a pirate ship. — This is the means by which the Original-Vow Dharma-door survives:
deception!
Buddhist disciples must open their eyes wide,

and whenever they encounter those organizations and websites that take the name “Pure Land school,” they must carefully distinguish whether or not it is the Original-Vow Dharma-door, so as not to be taken in

. The way to distinguish them is also simple: if it is led by Master Huijing, Master Jingzong, and others, advocating the views and theories of the Original-Vow Dharma-door — for example the Pure Land school Hongyuan Temple, the Pure Land school
Pure Land school Portal
China Pure Land school

Global Pure Land school Portal Website, the Chinese Pure Land school Association — these are the Original-Vow Dharma-door that attaches itself to Buddhism as an external way, and not the true Pure Land school,
their true name should be: the Original-Vow Dharma-door Hongyuan Temple, the China Original-Vow Dharma-door
Global Portal Website, the Chinese Original-Vow Dharma-door Association, and the like; only then would name and reality correspond

The ten schools: the Kośa school, the Satyasiddhi school, the Chan school, the Tiantai school, the Avataṃsaka school, the True Word school, the Dharma-character school, the Pure Land school, the Vinaya school, and the Three Treatises school.
